output.metric: The anomaly detector has reported nothing for a month
output.observed_change: A data quality detector has raised no alerts in 31 days, across a period that included two known incidents.
output.notes: The detector's own logs show healthy runs every hour.

blind_spots: No anomaly-detector, data-quality-monitor, or assertion entity is registered in the catalog under any searched term ('anomaly detector', 'data quality detector', 'assertion', 'monitor') — the detector named in the symptom is not itself represented in lineage, so its actual monitored input cannot be confirmed from metadata alone.
Only 11 of 24 upstream neighbours were enumerated by the lineage lookup; the remaining ~13 hop-1 nodes and all hop-2+ ancestors are unmapped.

Downstream includes a Snowflake replica (ORDER_DETAILS_REPLICA), several PowerBI datasets, Tableau custom SQL queries, and a Looker view, none of which have ownership or last-changed data recorded — if the detector actually watches one of these copies rather than the dbt view, sync staleness would be invisible from this metadata.

The schema lookup returned only free-text documentation with no field-level lineage, custom properties, or change-audit timestamps, so no schema-change history is available to correlate with the detector's silence.

output.statement: The anomaly detector is still executing hourly and logging 'healthy' runs, but a silent configuration or upstream-pointer defect (e.g., a stale table/view reference, a filter that now matches zero rows, or an evaluation window that never overlaps fresh data) causes it to evaluate an empty or frozen dataset every run, so it structurally cannot fire an alert regardless of real data quality — including during the two known incidents.
would_be_confirmed_by: The detector's query/config resolves to a table, partition, or column that has zero rows or has not been updated in the 31-day silence window
The detector's per-run row-count or input-hash metric is flat/zero across all runs in the window, including during the two known incidents
Re-pointing or correcting the detector's configuration to the live PROD dataset causes it to immediately raise alerts on historical replay of the incident windows
would_be_refuted_by: The detector's per-run logs show varying, non-zero row counts or input hashes that track known data volume changes across the 31-day window
The detector's resolved query/config target matches the live, actively-updated PROD dataset with no stale pointer or dead filter
Replaying the detector's exact logic against the two known-incident windows still fails to raise an alert even after confirming the input data was live and correctly scoped

output.statement: The detector's alerting configuration (severity threshold, notification routing, or channel binding) was silently changed at some point before the 31-day window, so the underlying assertion logic still evaluates hourly and may even internally flag both known incidents as anomalous, but those fires no longer produce a visible notification because they are filtered by a raised threshold, downgraded to informational, or routed to a disconnected/deprecated channel.
would_be_confirmed_by: Version/audit history of the assertion or monitor definition shows a change to severity, threshold, or notification-channel config prior to or during the 31-day window
Detector's internal run logs contain 'anomaly detected' or equivalent fire events during the two known incidents that have no corresponding entry in the notification/delivery log
The currently configured notification channel (Slack/email/PagerDuty endpoint) is found to be invalid, archived, or unsubscribed
would_be_refuted_by: The assertion/monitor configuration history shows no changes to threshold, severity, or notification routing across the entire lookback period
Internal run logs show the assertion evaluated to 'pass'/non-anomalous during both known incidents, not merely that a fired alert failed to notify
The configured notification channel shows successful, correctly-addressed delivery attempts at the time of the two incidents

output.statement: An upstream ingestion or transformation job feeding order_details (most likely orders, order_items, or products) silently stopped refreshing before the 31-day window began, so order_details has been serving a stale/frozen snapshot; the anomaly detector runs hourly and correctly finds no anomalies because the same unchanged data recurs every run, and the two known incidents never propagated into this frozen snapshot because their effects originated in upstream systems whose loads had already stopped reaching order_details.
would_be_confirmed_by: Upstream job run/orchestration logs (dbt run history for orders, order_items, or products) show the last successful data-changing run predates the 31-day window, with only no-op or failed runs since.
order_details (and its upstream sources) show a flat max(updated_at)/row-count/checksum across the entire 31-day window despite new orders existing in true source-of-record systems.
The timing of the pre-window last-successful-refresh aligns with or precedes the first of the two known incidents.
would_be_refuted_by: Row counts, max(updated_at), or content checksums for order_details or its upstream tables (orders, order_items, products, etc.) show measurable change/growth at multiple points within the 31-day window.
Upstream job logs show regular successful, data-changing runs (not just healthy no-op executions) throughout the window.
The two known incidents are shown to have altered rows that are present in order_details' current data (i.e., their effects did reach this dataset), which would rule out a freeze predating them.
